Thanks — I reviewed Claire's note and sketched a proposed paragraph and ops caveats you can share. Attaching a doc with tracked changes (proposed_dpa_redline_v2.docx). High-level answers and suggested contract text below.

High-level position (summary):
- Primary data and any system-of-record copies stored in the EU will be deleted within thirty (30) calendar days of a validated erase request, subject to the exceptions below.
- Encrypted snapshots and DR replicas maintained for disaster recovery are considered retained copies and will be destroyed within ninety (90) calendar days of a validated erase request unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Transient runtime artifacts (e.g., KV caches, ephemeral in-memory checkpoints) are not treated as retained backups and will be purged as part of normal garbage collection within seven (7) calendar days.

Proposed DPA clause (redline-ready):
"Data Deletion and Residual Copies — Subject to applicable law, upon Customer's verified request for deletion, Redwood will: (a) delete Customer Data from production storage within thirty (30) calendar days; (b) purge transient runtime artifacts and caches in the ordinary course of operations (typically within seven (7) calendar days); and (c) delete Disaster Recovery (DR) and backup snapshots that are preserved for resiliency purposes within ninety (90) calendar days. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may retain copies of Customer Data to the extent necessary to comply with law, to resolve disputes, enforce our agreements, or for bona fide archival or regulatory reasons, and Redwood will notify Customer and limit the scope of retained data to the minimum necessary."

Operational notes / questions for infra team:
- Marissa: confirm default DR snapshot replication targets for EU clusters and whether any cross-region copying to non-EU regions occurs for telemetry or support (we need this for the DPA).
- Encryption: confirm that DR snapshots use customer-key encryption where BYOK is configured; if not, we must call that out as a limitation.
- Forensic/legal hold flow: propose a standard SLA to respond to a hold request (acknowledge within 1 business day; timeline to produce or retain to be scoped case-by-case with legal).

If we're comfortable with 90 days for DR snapshots, I think this is defensible and similar to market practice; shorter windows (30 days across all copies) will be hard for resilience. Let me know if you want alternate language for negotiation (e.g., 60 days or carve-outs for cold long-term backups).

Claire — thanks for the clear list. See answers below and attached proposed DPA language (proposed_dpa_redline_v2.docx) per Laura. Short answers first:

1) Scope of 30-day deletion: primary production storage only.
2) Backups/DR snapshots: considered retained copies; proposed retention 90 days to allow for safe restore and DR testing.
3) Runtime KV caches/checkpoints: treated as transient and garbage-collected (typical purge within 7 days).
4) Cross-border replication: default EU clusters do not replicate customer data outside EU regions unless explicitly enabled for a customer DR program; telemetry and aggregated logs exclude customer content.

Proposed resolution path:
- We are proposing the DPA paragraph Laura drafted (attached). If Nova needs a shorter window for DR snapshots, we can propose 60 days and include a documented operational runbook that explains recovery and risk tradeoffs.
- Forholds/forensics: standard process would be to acknowledge an evidence or hold request within 1 business day and agree a scoped retention timeline; extraordinary holds (e.g., regulatory investigations) would be escalated to legal and may require separate agreement.

Open items for us to confirm before we hand this to Nova legal:
- Marissa: confirm by EOD whether any platform telemetry or third-party backup providers maintain copies outside EU for support purposes.
- Security: confirm encryption-at-rest and whether BYOK applies to DR snapshots (if the customer requires BYOK we should call that out).

If that looks acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute call with Nova legal tomorrow to agree final wording? Claire — are you available Thu 14 Oct in the afternoon CET?

Thanks,
